invariant: Every refused oversized event-batch upload receives its governed 413 BATCH_FRAMING_REFUSED response; mid-stream refusal followed by body drain must leave the connection usable for subsequent requests.
reproduction: Unskip the single it block in tests/rfl-oversize-upload-connection.test.ts, then run: npm run test:integration -- tests/rfl-oversize-upload-connection.test.ts
paths: src/governance-service/GovernanceHttpService.ts (ingestBatch framing, readIncomingBody size refusal, post-refusal resume drain)
src/governance-service/server-entry.ts (combined server without timeout envelope; contrast createGovernanceHttpServer)
observed: Refused multi-MB uploads intermittently receive a transport error (ECONNRESET via undici keep-alive reuse) instead of the governed 413: 2.4MB bodies 4/10 failures, 5.1MB bodies 4/10 failures across consecutive runs, 2.05MB bodies 0/10. Empty and small requests always receive governed responses. Service stays healthy throughout; rate limiting unaffected. Prime suspect (hypothesis, not established): the post-refusal resume() drain races the client's still-transmitting upload and the socket is destroyed, poisoning the pooled connection for the next request that draws it.
notes: RFL recorded only; no production code changed. Skipped reproducer committed alongside for independent rerun after any transport fix.

invariant: Service stop() resolves boundedly while uploads are stalled mid-body; the forced-shutdown path releases connections it cannot drain.
reproduction: Unskip the single it block in tests/rfl-shutdown-drain.test.ts, then run: npm run test:integration -- tests/rfl-shutdown-drain.test.ts
paths: src/governance-service/server-entry.ts (runGovernanceService shutdown: server.close then closeStorage, 5s forced timer sets exitCode only)
src/governance-service/GovernanceHttpService.ts (no request ceiling on the combined entry server; contrast createGovernanceHttpServer timeouts)
observed: stop() with two uploads stalled mid-body is still pending past a 4s bound on two consecutive runs (control: idle stop resolves promptly). server.close() waits indefinitely for the never-completing uploads while the forced path only sets process.exitCode without destroying sockets, so SIGTERM during stalled uploads hangs the process past its own shutdown deadline.
notes: RFL recorded only; no production code changed. Skipped reproducer committed alongside for independent rerun after any shutdown-drain fix.

invariant: Concurrent key resolutions share a single in-flight discovery-plus-JWKS refresh round instead of stampeding the identity provider.
reproduction: Unskip the single it block in tests/rfl-jwks-refresh-coalescing.test.ts, then run: npm run test:integration -- tests/rfl-jwks-refresh-coalescing.test.ts
paths: src/governance-service/OidcJwksAuthority.ts (resolveForVerification checks a possibly-stale cache with no in-flight refresh coalescing)
observed: Three concurrent resolveForVerification calls on a cold cache issue three full refresh rounds (6 fetches: 3 discovery plus 3 JWKS) instead of one shared round (2 fetches). Sequential resolutions correctly reuse the cache (2 fetches total), so the defect is the missing in-flight coalescing, not absent caching. Every returned key is still correct; the impact is N-fold request amplification toward the OIDC provider on cold start and cache expiry, plus tail latency on all but the first completer.
notes: RFL recorded only; no production code changed. Skipped reproducer committed alongside for independent rerun after in-flight refresh coalescing lands.

invariant: Within one synchronous emit, removal of a handler (once wrapper retirement or mid-dispatch off) must not suppress delivery to other still-registered handlers; dispatch order must be the registration order of handlers present at emit start.
reproduction: Unskip the two it blocks in tests/rfl-eventbus-dispatch-skip.test.ts, then run: npm run test:integration -- tests/rfl-eventbus-dispatch-skip.test.ts
paths: src/utils/EventBus.ts (_emitCore iterates the live _handlers list; _offCore splices it mid-iteration; once wrapper always off-splices before invoking the handler)
observed: once + later handler: later handler called 0 times on first emit. Self-off mid-dispatch: successor handler called 0 times. Dispatch-order contract in EventBus.ts doc comment is violated. Deterministic pure-function case; two reduced runs agree. Fix direction (snapshot list at emit start) is hypothesis, not established.
notes: RFL recorded only; no production code changed. Skipped reproducers committed alongside for independent rerun after snapshot-dispatch lands.
